title: The final hybrid is the right family
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\Omega$ be a type, and let $Z$ assign a real-valued function on $\Omega$ to each element of the disjoint union of two copies of the $n$-coordinate set. The hybrid family at stage $n$ equals the family whose coordinate $i$ is the function assigned by $Z$ to the right copy of $i$.
hypotheses_covered: $Z$ is a family of real-valued functions indexed by two disjoint copies of the $n$-coordinate set
replaced: Let $Z_{L,i},Z_{R,i}\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be two families indexed by $0\le i<n$, and define $H^{(r)}_i=Z_{R,i}$ if $i<r$ and $Z_{L,i}$ otherwise. Then $H^{(n)}_i=Z_{R,i}$ for every $i$, including the empty family when $n=0$.
